newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil seen $2-$3 higher on US weather, Iran.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil seen $2-$3 higher on US weather, Iran.

text.p: IPE Brent futures were called to open unchanged to five cents higher on Thursday while May gas oil was called $2 to $3 higher on fundamental news, traders said. Brokers said the market could get a shot in the arm from news that a new cold spell would affect the United States and news of a row between Germany and Iran over the killing of Kurdish exiles. "Last night there was a fair amount of technical buying and I think some of the funds were panicked as they got a short covering...I think some of the hedge funds would start to buy back," one broker said.

Brokers said the market will be watching to see if the Germany-Iran row worsens. Germany had ordered four Iranian diplomats to leave the country after a Berlin court decision implicating Tehran in the 1992 killings of four Kurdish dissidents in a Berlin restaurant.
The European Union invited member countries to recall their ambassadors from Iran for consultations. Tehran responded by withdrawing its ambassador from Germany and expelling four German diplomats.
"The market is watching the Iran-Germany situation to see how it develops," one broker said.

While the dispute would have no immediate impact on oil supply from Iran, an OPEC member and the world's third largest oil exporter after Saudi Arabia and Norway, it could force the EU to drop its opposition to U.S. trade sanctions against Tehran, analysts said.
Attempts to improve relations between Iran and its Gulf neighbours could also suffer, they said.
May gas oil, which became the prompt contact after April expired on Thursday, closed $3.75 lower at $160.50 a tonne, just 75 cents off the session low.
May Brent futures closed 18 cents higher at $17.95 a barrle, after dipping to a new nine-month low of $17.54 a barrel in mid-afternoon dealing on Thursday.
